about: Cases SeedSigner 5f321768 (embit 0.8.0) fails, each with the code that decides it. These are findings, not waivers, and several are questions for the profile rather than faults in SeedSigner: the profile is a draft, and where SeedSigner made a deliberate, documented choice the reason says so. The runner fails if any of these starts passing, so the list follows SeedSigner as it changes.

failures.reason: 100 rolls cannot be entered: ToolsDiceEntropyEntryView returns after exactly 50 or 99 (views/tools_views.py line 275, helpers/mnemonic_generation.py lines 17-18). The encoding is the profile's, SHA-256 of the ASCII rolls; only the count differs. Open question for the profile: 99 rolls give 255.91 bits
As published-worked-example: the entry screen takes exactly 99 rolls for 24 words
As published-worked-example: no count other than 50 or 99 can be entered

99 rolls is SeedSigner's 24-word count (DICE__NUM_ROLLS__24WORD), which the profile refuses because floor(99 log2 6) is 255 bits. The same question as above, from the other side

Not the ownership rule: the case's owned input is taproot and its foreign input segwit v0, and PSBTParser refuses any transaction whose inputs resolve to different policies (models/psbt_parser.py line 703). A TODO beside it (lines 699-702) says the policy should come from the user's own inputs alone, since BIP-174 and BIP-78 allow such a spend

By design: PSBTParser.trim returns a new PSBT holding only the unsigned transaction and each input's signatures or final witness (models/psbt_parser.py lines 1224-1236), so the signed QR is small and the coordinator combines. Open question for the profile: whether a signer that returns only its signatures meets SP-REV-11

embit 0.8.0 signs BIP-340 with no aux_rand at all, deriving the nonce from the key unmasked (embit/util/key.py sign_schnorr when aux is None; its bundled libsecp256k1 does the same). BIP-340 masks the key with hash_BIP0340/aux(a) for a 32-byte a, and Bitcoin Core 31.1 signs with a of 32 zero bytes, so Core cannot reproduce these signatures. They are valid and deterministic

Not the signature rule: PSBTParser refuses any transaction whose inputs resolve to different policies (models/psbt_parser.py line 703), and these inputs are segwit v0 and taproot. Its ECDSA signatures in the other cases match the low-R bytes

Deliberate and documented: PSBTParser asks for PSBT_IN_NON_WITNESS_UTXO only on inputs whose sighash commits no amount (models/psbt_parser.py lines 315-320 and 640-646). Lines 577-595 give the reason, that a false segwit v0 amount invalidates the signature rather than spending more, and accept the attack that leaves open when a multi-input transaction is signed more than once (CVE-2020-14199), because coordinators seldom send a QR signer the previous transaction. It has no override to hold the input behind. The profile treats that amount as the coordinator's word (BIP-174 line 415); which is right is a question for the profile's review
Follows from without-override: it signs the third time for the same reason it signed the first, not because an override was kept

The change screen draws the address on one line as its first and last seven characters around "..." (gui/screens/psbt_screens.py lines 714-717, gui/components.py lines 951-983), beside "Address verified!" (psbt_screens.py lines 720-748), so the full address is never shown. SeedSigner has already proved the output is the seed's by re-deriving its script (models/psbt_parser.py lines 1009-1019 and 1070-1090). SP-REV-5 says no address may be elided; whether a re-derived change address must be shown in full is a question for the profile

The change screen shows the branch and the last index, "change address #0" (gui/screens/psbt_screens.py lines 693-704), not the path. The full path is passed to the screen (views/psbt_views.py line 507) and not drawn. SP-REV-6 asks for the path beside the output

PSBTParser looks for change only among outputs whose script type matches the inputs' (_is_change_candidate, models/psbt_parser.py lines 979 and 1372-1415). This wallet spends a p2wpkh input to a p2tr change address, so the change is shown as a payment, with its full address. The cautious direction; the vector expects every output the seed re-derives to be change. A p2wpkh output at that path would not be change either: the change path rules refuse the transaction, since no input spends from m/86'/0'/0' (lines 1900-1902 and 1995-1996)

SeedSigner checks for change only at the path an output's derivation record names, and with no record, "There's nothing for us to verify against so this output will be considered an external spend" (models/psbt_parser.py lines 1015-1023). The record cannot make an output change by itself, since the script is re-derived and compared (lines 1070-1090), but it decides which outputs are checked. SP-REV-6 says no PSBT field may contribute to the change label

Not the fee rule: the inputs are segwit v0 and taproot, and PSBTParser refuses any transaction whose inputs resolve to different policies (models/psbt_parser.py line 703). PSBTOverviewView does not catch that RuntimeError (views/psbt_views.py lines 110-209), so it ends at the System Error screen (controller.py lines 324-328)
Follows from verdict: no review is shown

As segwit-v0-witness-utxo-only. Two inputs, one with no previous transaction, is the case lines 582-595 accept by name (CVE-2020-14199). Both are at m/84'/0'/0', so the rule against segwit v0 inputs from several base paths without previous transactions (lines 2076-2101) does not apply

The review shows no sighash, and Approve signs: embit signs the input asking for ALL and skips the one asking for SINGLE (embit/psbt.py lines 969-977), and PSBTFinalizeView counts one new signature and shows the signed QR (views/psbt_views.py lines 1139-1151). Nothing says the second input was left unsigned
No screen shows nLockTime: nothing under src/seedsigner reads it (the review is views/psbt_views.py lines 97-1196)
No screen shows whether the transaction signals replaceability: nothing under src/seedsigner reads an input's nSequence

SeedSigner sends a UR frame to its PSBT decoder only when it begins UR:CRYPTO-PSBT/ (models/decode_qr.py lines 348-349). UR:PSBT/ matches no QR type, and the scan ends at "Unknown QR Type" (views/scan_views.py lines 163-167). The profile records this itself: SP-TX-7 says SeedSigner reads only crypto-psbt

SeedSigner reads BBQr only as a PSBT: a frame goes to its BBQr decoder only when it matches B$[2HZ]P (models/decode_qr.py lines 366-367), and this scan is file type U, so it ends at "Unknown QR Type" (views/scan_views.py lines 163-167). It reads encoding Z, which reference-Z-psbt checks; only the file type differs

SeedSigner keeps the first copy of each part and ignores any later copy without comparing it (models/decode_qr.py lines 673-685), so the transfer completes. Here the first copy is the genuine one and the PSBT assembled is the one sent; whichever copy arrives first is the one used. Coinkite's reference join raises on these frames

embit 0.8.0 parses PSBT_GLOBAL_UNSIGNED_TX with Transaction.parse (psbt.py line 775) and checks neither of BIP-174's rules on it (line 102: empty scriptSigs and witnesses, the old serialization), so the PSBT parses and, with an input the seed owns, reaches PSBTOverviewView like any other. embit's master (2b375a3, after 0.8.0) now rejects a non-empty scriptSig, so a SeedSigner release on a newer embit would pass this case. The same rule fails BIP-174's own vector for it, which embit's tests on master still carry commented out as failing.

embit 0.8.0 parses PSBT_GLOBAL_UNSIGNED_TX with Transaction.parse (psbt.py line 775) and checks neither of BIP-174's rules on it (line 102: empty scriptSigs and witnesses, the old serialization), so the PSBT parses and, with an input the seed owns, reaches PSBTOverviewView like any other. Transaction.read_from takes a zero input count for the segwit marker (transaction.py line 150), so the marker, flag and empty witness are read as segwit. Still so on embit's master (2b375a3), where the same detection also rejects BIP-174's two valid PSBTs with no inputs.

PSBTParser keeps an OP_RETURN output only as its payload (models/psbt_parser.py lines 1188-1190, and only the last such output's), and PSBTOpReturnView shows that payload as text or hex, with no amount and no output number (views/psbt_views.py lines 1083-1108). No screen lists the output or its script. Whether a payload read correctly from every push encoding, as it is since SeedSigner #1042, meets "its script" is a question for the profile; the missing amount is not.

It is added to no total (lines 1188-1211), so PSBTMathView's input, spend, fee and change (views/psbt_views.py lines 347-352) no longer sum, and the amount destroyed is shown nowhere.
